quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 34

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the lane you want to enter is a ____ line.

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: What can help you prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid stopping suddenly.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal before braking.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops are dangerous. When stopping, release the gas pedal first to let your car slow down. Then press the brake pedal smoothly. This turns on your brake lights and gives cars behind you time to react.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line separating traffic mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both lanes go in the same direction.
You may not pass.
You may pass even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means both directions can pass. You may only pass if no oncoming cars are coming.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Move to the right side and stop.
Stop right where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, pull over to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the roadway, what should you do?

options.text: No action is needed.
Honk your horn.
Pass as close to the animal as possible.
Be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Always be careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass slowly to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line, with the broken line next to your lane, you may pass:

options.text: Only in an emergency.
Only on an expressway.
If traffic is clear.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: If traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line and the broken line is next to your lane, you may cross to pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You may drive across a dashed white line:

options.text: At any time.
Only during daylight hours.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes going the same direction. You may cross them to pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes if possible so you do not drive next to it.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and drive at the same speed.
Speed up to pass quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes if possible so you do not drive next to it.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, slow down and move to another lane if you can do so safely. If there is only one lane in your direction, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much space as possible. Always be ready to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A crossroad is ahead.
A flagger is ahead.
A lane ends.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about road hazards ahead. This sign warns you that an intersection is coming.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate with each other.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: Vehicles at a four-way stop normally go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: When a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.
Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: Traffic lights help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers must obey traffic signals, except when a police officer is directing traffic. In that case, follow the officer's directions.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.
The car on the left has the right-of-way.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at the same time at an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The left driver can then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other cars.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out quickly to merge with traffic.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and roadway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and roadway traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you. Your headlights should be:

options.text: On high beam.
On low beam.
Off. Use your parking lights instead.
On either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: On low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when approaching or following another vehicle at night. Use low beam to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: Never.
When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles go first when they are using flashing lights or a siren.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross first. Watch carefully for pedestrians at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop and back up immediately.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn that work is being done on or near the roadway. Be very careful when you see these signs.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you. What must you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until the vehicle passes you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the nearest roadside and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches on a one-way street, move to the nearest roadside and stop.

questions.question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best thing to do?

options.text: Get out of the car and go look for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car because rescuers are more likely to find you there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car because rescuers are more likely to find you there.
questions.explanation: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. Rescuers are more likely to find you if you stay with your vehicle. It is also safer than walking in a snowstorm.

questions.question: What is a "No zone"?

options.text: A blind spot around a truck or bus where you cannot be seen.
A special speed zone.
A roadway with rules about vehicle stereo volume.
A TV show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A blind spot around a truck or bus where you cannot be seen.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on the sides, rear, and front. Your car cannot be seen in these areas. These blind spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must stay within 12 inches of the road edge.

questions.question: How should you prepare for hazards ahead on the road?

options.text: Look at the entire road and all roadsides constantly.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot resting on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all roadsides constantly.
questions.explanation: Handling dangerous situations depends on spotting problems before you reach them. Do not just stare at the center of the road. Scan the entire road, including both sides.

questions.question: What should you do while backing up?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: Possible speeds for the area.
The fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest speed you are allowed to drive.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the maximum or minimum safe speed allowed on a road. These limits are for ideal conditions. You must slow down when conditions are worse.

questions.question: Why is leaving space around your vehicle important?

options.text: It prevents other vehicles from distracting you.
It gives you time to react to surprises.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.
It keeps other drivers alert.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to surprises.
questions.explanation: Leaving plenty of space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pick-up truck.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have any open alcoholic beverage in a vehicle on a public road. You cannot store open alcohol containers in any part of the vehicle that passengers occupy.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
How the road surface is.

questions.correctAnswerText: How the road surface is.
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects how fast you can stop. Slow down when roads are wet or slippery to stay in control. Driving too fast on slippery roads puts you at risk.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Use different routes.
Drive the same way you would on dry roads.
Stay farther behind the car ahead.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car ahead.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between you and the car in front. Your vehicle may take longer to stop than on normal roads.

questions.question: What does this sign show?

options.text: A right turn.
An intersection.
A lane change.
A road curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: Which substances can impair your driving and result in a DUII arrest?

options.text: Beer, wine, and other alcohol
Illegal drugs or prescription medicines
Inhalants like glue or paint
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications (prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must allow for:

options.text: The longer distance large vehicles need to stop.
The shorter distance large vehicles need to stop.
The quieter sound of large vehicles.
The higher speed of large vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer distance large vehicles need to stop.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where your view of traffic is not blocked.

questions.question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is divided by ____ lines.

options.text: White
Red
Black
Yellow

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane to pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed ahead to pass quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of space. Bicyclists have little protection. Passing too quickly can force them off course.

questions.question: Orange signs are:

options.text: Work zone signs.
Regulatory signs.
School zone signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are diamond-shaped, orange, and have black letters or symbols. They warn that people are working on or near the highway.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No right turns.
Right turns are permitted.
Stop before turning right.
Sharp curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash means a specific action is prohibited. Right turns are not allowed where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Which of the following helps direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows show which lanes to use for specific purposes, such as driving straight or turning.

questions.question: Night driving requires more caution because:

options.text: Traffic moves faster at night.
There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well. You must use headlights from one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise, or when vehicles cannot be seen for 500 feet.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other:

options.text: It is always safe to cross after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing.
Look for another train on the other track after one train passes.
Honk your horn as you cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for another train on the other track after one train passes.
questions.explanation: When one train passes, check for another train on the second track. Do not cross until you are sure no train is approaching on either track.

questions.question: When you see this sign, you must:

options.text: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
Slow down without stopping.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and check for pedestrians and cross traffic.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely, check for pedestrians and cross traffic, and wait for the intersection to clear before going.
